liam: Heads-up — saw a 2.3x p99 regression on the short-seqlen path after enabling graph capture + inductor on the latest runtime build. nvprof/nsys shows a kernel swap around step ~40.

sophie: ouch. which kernel swapped? matmul->tensorcore? :eyes:

liam: Not tensorcore per se — it switched from our seqlen-aware fused matmul+attn kernel to a conservative fallback GEMM kernel that has worse launch/streaming characteristics. nvtx timeline attached.

marco: can you paste the nsys snippet and the capture command? also did KV cache warmup change anything? sometimes odd offsets alter capture shape.

liam: repro steps below. staging, batch=8, seqlen=32->64 warmup mix, torch.compile (inductor) + cudaGraphCapture=on.
```
# repro (staging)
export CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0
python -m torchbench.run --model t5-lm --batch 8 --seq-len 32 --warmup 40 --steps 120 \
  --compile=inductor --cuda-graph=1 --runtime-build=rl-deploy-2026-03
nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx --output=~/profiles/run1 ./run_repro.sh
```

liam: nsys timeline excerpt: (trimmed)
```
[40s] graph-capture:start
[41s] kernel:start  matmul_seqlen32_fused  gpu=0 time=0.42ms
[42s] kernel:end    matmul_seqlen32_fused
[43s] kernel:start  gemm_fallback_generic  gpu=0 time=1.02ms
[44s] kernel:end    gemm_fallback_generic
```

devx-ana: That looks like a kernel-picker heuristic flip. The autotuner probably saw shape variance during capture and chose a safe kernel for the captured graph. Does the runtime log show an autotune decision at step ~40? try enabling debug=kernelpicker.

liam: enabled debug logs, snippet: 
```
[runtime] 2026-03-12T14:12:39Z pick_kernel(model=t5, seqlen=32, batch=8) -> matmul_seqlen32_fused (score=12.3)
[runtime] 2026-03-12T14:12:40Z capture: graph_shape=(32,8) observed_variance=0.12
[runtime] 2026-03-12T14:12:40Z pick_kernel(model=t5, seqlen=64, batch=8) -> gemm_fallback_generic (score=14.1)
```

marco: observed_variance=0.12 — meaning the seqlen bumped to 64 during capture. Could be KV-cache replay or a prompt prefix causing a transient. If graph capture sees mixed shapes it picks the safest kernel to keep graph stable. But that fallback has terrible per-token throughput for short sequences.

sophie: hmm, why would seqlen go to 64 mid-capture? our batching heuristic should pin seqlen groups. are you running the new dynamic-batcher patch?

liam: yes, staging has dynamic-batcher v2 (shape coalescing) enabled. It coalesces recently seen prefixes into the active capture group. If a rare long prefix arrives during warmup it can expand the capture shape.

devx-ana: proposed mitigation: (1) make capture use the modal shape instead of max-observed, (2) add a guard that if chosen kernel regresses p99 by >1.2x on short path, force recompile with preferred kernel.

marco: agree. another quick win: when KV replay is used, prefer replay-only capture that pins cache offsets. Also we could add an autotune cost model term for launch overhead to penalize fallback kernels on short seqlen.

liam: i ran a quick experiment: forcing kernel_picker to prefer matmul_seqlen32_fused during capture -> p99 returns to baseline. so it's definitely just a heuristic prioritization issue.

sophie: can you throw the small reproducer into a CI perf test and tag me? i'll draft a patch for the picker change. also add a nsys snapshot to the PR.

liam: will do. attaching compressed profile (5MB) to the ticket and creating the perf CI run.

devx-ana: FYI we should also check how this interacts with cudaGraph streaming groups — captured graph may embed kernel IDs and the kernel registry lookup must be stable across captures. if registry ordering differs, you can get different kernels bound at replay time.

marco: good call — ordering nondeterminism could surface when two kernels have similar scores. add a deterministic tie-break (arch, score, kernel_id) in the picker.

liam: noted. next steps: (1) perf CI reproducer + profile (on me), (2) devx patch to picker + modal-shape capture fallback, (3) add unit that simulates KV offset churn and ensures capture doesn't expand shape unexpectedly.

sophie: sounds good. tag me on PRs and i'll review the picker heuristics. :thumbsup:

liam: thanks — will follow up with links when CI finishes.
